content: The metabolism of ketamine can be influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which may alter its levels or effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Conversely, ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ketamine through the same mechanism, necessitating similar precautions. Ketoconazole increases lopinavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Similarly, ketoconazole increases ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, requiring therapy adjustments and monitoring. Ritonavir raises lacosamide levels through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of toxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are essential, and alternatives should be considered if available. Lopinavir also increases lacosamide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating dose adjustments and monitoring. When co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, the lacosamide dose may need to be reduced. Ritonavir and lamivudine both elevate the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome, requiring caution and monitoring. Lopinavir reduces lamotrigine levels by increasing its metabolism, potentially decreasing lamotrigine levels by up to 50%. Dose adjustments for lamotrigine are necessary when starting, stopping, or changing lopinavir/ritonavir doses. Ritonavir similarly decreases lamotrigine levels, requiring caution and monitoring. Lapatinib increases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lenacapavir also raises ritonavir and lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, with potential risks of adverse reactions for up to nine months after the last subcutaneous dose. Monitoring is essential. Lopinavir and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating ECG monitoring and caution. Ritonavir increases letermovir levels by reducing its metabolism, while letermovir raises ritonavir and lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy adjustments and monitoring are required. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase levamlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reductions may be necessary when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. Monitoring for hypotension and edema is recommended. Ritonavir increases levocetirizine levels by reducing its metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Levoketoconazole raises lopinavir and ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Therapy adjustments and monitoring are necessary, and ketoconazole doses above 200 mg/day are not recommended with lopinavir/ritonavir. Lopinavir increases levomilnacipran levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The dose of levomilnacipran should not exceed 80 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ritonavir similarly increases levomilnacipran levels, requiring therapy adjustments and monitoring. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase linagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism but may reduce its effects due to insulin resistance. Monitoring is advised. Similar effects are observed with liraglutide, with reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Ritonavir increases lofepramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Lopinavir and lofexidine both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating ECG monitoring. Ritonavir also increases lofexidine levels via CYP2D6 inhibition, and dose reductions may be needed. Lomitapide increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring therapy adjustments and monitoring. Ritonavir raises loperamide levels through the same mechanism, necessitating caution. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase loratadine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is advised. Lorlatinib reduces lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Ritonavir increases losartan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose adjustments may be required when initiating therapy with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase lumateperone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reductions to 5 mg/day may be necessary with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Lopinavir may also alter lumefantrine levels, requiring caution. Ritonavir increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. The maraviroc dose should be reduced to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Ritonavir increases marijuana levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while marijuana raises ritonavir and lopinavir levels through the same mechanism. Monitoring is advised. Mavorixafor increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and prolongs the QTc interval. Therapy adjustments and monitoring are necessary. Lopinavir increases medroxyprogesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase meperidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of toxicity. Monitoring is essential. Ritonavir increases mestranol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition but may also reduce its levels by increasing metabolism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Ritonavir reduces metformin effects due to insulin resistance, requiring monitoring. Ritonavir may also induce methadone metabolism, reducing its effects. Monitoring is advised. Ritonavir increases methylprednisolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, with potential risks of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Monitoring is essential. Ritonavir increases metoprolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, requiring caution. Metronidazole raises lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating monitoring. Ritonavir increases mexiletine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, requiring monitoring for toxicity. Dose reductions may be necessary. Miconazole vaginal increases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Ritonavir increases midazolam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating monitoring. Mifepristone raises ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and prolongs the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended. Mifepristone doses should not exceed 300 mg/day for Cushing's syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Ritonavir reduces miglitol effects due to insulin resistance, requiring monitoring. Ritonavir and mipomersen both increase each other's toxicity, necessitating liver function monitoring. Mirabegron increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, requiring caution. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase mirtazapine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of toxicity. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase mirvetuximab soravtansine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing adverse reactions. Monitoring is advised. Mitotane reduces lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and dose adjustments may be necessary. Ritonavir increases momelotinib toxicity by inhibiting OATP1B1/B3 transporters, requiring monitoring. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase mometasone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Ritonavir increases morphine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, requiring caution. Lopinavir increases naldemedine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein transporters, necessitating monitoring. Nafcillin reduces ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Lopinavir reduces nateglinide effects due to insulin resistance, necessitating monitoring. Ritonavir increases nebivolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, requiring caution. Nefazodone raises lopinavir and ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating monitoring. Ritonavir increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitoring is advised. Lopinavir increases netupitant/palonosetron levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring therapy adjustments. Nevirapine reduces lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating monitoring. Ritonavir increases nicardipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring caution. Nifedipine raises lopinavir and ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating monitoring. Nilotinib increases lopinavir and ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein transporters, requiring caution. Lopinavir increases nimodipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating monitoring. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase nintedanib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring therapy adjustments. Lopinavir increases nisoldipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating monitoring.
